note: How strict each phase gate is (EE-156). Each gate item names what proves it and how its strength is measured on the evidence levels (adapted from GRADE: very low, low, moderate, high). A policy sets, per item, the minimum level and the boundary: fail-closed refuses the phase change, fail-open lets it pass and names the shortfall as an open risk. Three presets rank from lenient to strict; a venture picks one, and may tune items, under phase_gates in naive.config.json. Every threshold here is an unvalidated prior, ours.
count_note: Counted evidence (interviews) maps to a level by these minimum counts: about ten interviews is Blank's customer discovery guidance; five is the grader's minimum sample.

items.label: A named customer
items.ask: Who has the problem, specifically enough to find more of them?

items.label: A real problem
items.ask: Is the problem frequent or painful enough that people already try to solve it?

items.label: Current alternatives
items.ask: How do they cope today, and why does that fall short?

items.label: A solution that fits
items.ask: Does a solution fit the problem well enough to test it with those people?

items.label: A way to reach them
items.ask: Has at least one channel produced conversations with them?

items.label: An economic signal
items.ask: Who would pay, and is there a sign that a budget exists?

items.label: A validation plan
items.ask: Which assumptions are still open, and how will each be tested?

items.label: A decision
items.ask: Has a person weighed the evidence and chosen to go on?
